# C1 — Folding-fin mechanism model

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | **SUPPORTED WITHIN STATED LIMITS** — Evidence supports the statement as worded, at its evidence class only. |
| Strongest accepted evidence | MODEL ONLY |
| Evidence classes cited | IMPLEMENTATION, TEST PROCEDURE, ANALYTICAL |
| Gate reached | ANALYTICAL MODEL (next: SOFTWARE REPRODUCTION) |
| Last review | CURRENT — human recorded 2026-11-14 by chief weapons engineer |

**Question.** Can the four-bar linkage carry the fin from folded flush to its 90 deg stop and lock it over-center against fin loads?

**Current statement.** The historical linkage (ground 25, coupler 60, input 15, output 15 mm) closed at no pose (D-002) and is kept as the failure record. The Phase 1 militarized redesign (ground 25, crank 14, coupler 15.5, output 15 mm, from design_point.json) closes at every pose of the deployment stroke, deploys the fin monotonically from flush to the 90 deg stop, and places the linkage toggle 1.5 deg beyond the stop: at the stop the back-drive ratio is 0.363, so fin hinge moments reach the crank attenuated and the spring preload holds the fin on its stop. Worst-case plus/minus 0.15 mm link tolerances still assemble at the stop. All of this is analytical kinematics; no physical mechanism has been observed.

## Discrepancies

- [D-002](../DISCREPANCIES.md#d-002) (RESOLVED) The specified four-bar cannot be assembled
- [D-003](../DISCREPANCIES.md#d-003) (RESOLVED) C1 model revision 1 reported placeholders as results, and its tests passed on them
- [D-004](../DISCREPANCIES.md#d-004) (RESOLVED) Over-center locking is claimed but not modeled
- [D-005](../DISCREPANCIES.md#d-005) (RESOLVED) C1 CAD artifacts are illustrative bars, not the modeled mechanism

## Assumptions

- The mechanism is a planar, pin-jointed four-bar loop.
- Link lengths are pin-centre distances in millimetres.
- The assembly branch is tracked by continuity of joint C, as a physical pin-jointed mechanism does.

## Limitations

- Kinematics say nothing about joint friction (modeled statistically in C7), link compliance, or impact loads at the stop.
- Rendered or exported CAD of the links is not evidence that a physical mechanism assembles.
- The over-center lock is modeled (back-drive ratio and tolerance sweep); the holding-moment requirement is still a physical test.

## Measurement needed to close the next gate

- An inert, instrumented deployment test of a printed or machined linkage at the militarized dimensions.
- Stop-angle and toggle-position as-built measurement.

## Pre-registered experiments

- None.

## What this claim does not establish

- Any inert physical measurement: none has been accepted for this claim.
- Physical performance of any hardware.
- Flight readiness or safety for live propulsion.
